case.description: Design a removable joint for a 300 mm inspection hatch on a dry tabletop trough fixture. A technician must open it repeatedly while retaining the existing hatch, rim and seal. All dimensions and observations below are stipulated for this hypothetical fixture.
case.valued_outcome: After ten opening cycles, the closed hatch stays within 1 mm of its marked position, withstands a supplied 20 N sideways pull, and can be reopened by one technician within 30 seconds.
hard_constraints: Do not drill, cut, glue or permanently deform the hatch or trough.
Keep the full marked inspection opening unobstructed when open.
Use no powered mechanism; loose components must remain recoverable.
The seal must show no new visible tears after testing.
resources: One 300 by 180 mm hatch, one trough rim and one 2 mm removable seal.
Four 100 by 25 by 3 mm aluminum strips, two 250 mm fabric straps, six M4 bolts with nuts, four rubber pads and 1 m of cord.
One hand drill usable only on supplied strips, one hacksaw, two spanners, ruler and marker.
Ninety minutes for fabrication and twenty minutes for observation.
observations: The untreated hatch slides 4 mm under the 20 N pull.
The seal leaves a continuous contact mark when the hatch is centered.
Awkward observation: pressing the hatch more tightly at its left corner makes the opposite corner lift 2 mm; this occurred in three supplied trials.

openings.claim: Use the known strap separation-retention function alone: two removable fabric straps across the hatch carry tension to padded, bolted paired-strip rim clamps. No spacer function is proposed.
openings.delta: Change the retention carrier from an ordinary cord lash to fabric straps attached to removable strip clamps. Release and move the entire assembly beside the trough for inspection; recover all components. Clamp attachment, strap reach and unobstructed removal remain unproved.
openings.prediction: If balanced strap tension retains the hatch without reproducing the opposite-corner lift, it may also resist sideways motion through existing contact friction. Against a cord lash on the same anchors, compare marked displacement, corner lift, release time and visible seal damage. Wider strap contact might reduce concentrated loading; superiority and adequate friction are uncertain.
openings.probe: First check actual rim access, strap reach, reversible padded clamping and clear removal using supplied parts. Stop if these fail or damage appears. Fabricate within ninety minutes. Allocate ten closure/pull trials to the strap configuration, checking position, 20 N resistance, reopening time and seal after every cycle; use the right-contact card on trial ten. Allocate two trials to the ordinary cord rival, one normal and one disturbed. Complete observations within twenty minutes; count every closure/pull toward twelve. The rival receives only an exploratory comparison, not ten-cycle qualification.
assumptions: Rim geometry permits padded reversible clamps, which must be established rather than assumed.
The supplied straps reach and can be secured and released with supplied bolts; cord length suffices for the rival and recoverability.

Defeat conditions include insufficient reach or anchor capacity, corner lift, movement beyond 1 mm, failure under 20 N, reopening beyond 30 seconds, obstruction or new seal tears. Stop caps do not establish feasibility.

artifact.assessment: This is a bounded probe, not a deployment claim. Preserve the existing hatch, rim and seal without drilling, cutting, gluing or permanent deformation. All outcomes remain required after ten cycles and the disturbed final closure; only seal-contact continuity is exempted. Unknown geometry and retention capacity prevent a preserves verdict.

openings.claim: Removable rim clips could carry sideways load through hatch-edge stops while applying only enough vertical retention to prevent escape, reducing dependence on seal friction.
openings.delta: Change the load carrier from increased corner pressure to lateral bearing. Make two opposed clip assemblies from paired supplied strips, bolts and padded jaws; locate their bolt shanks as hatch-edge stops only if actual rim access and hatch geometry permit. Remove the clips completely before inspection; tether them externally with the supplied cord.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, stronger corner clamping, lightly retained positive stops should resist the 20 N pull without requiring the pressure increase associated with opposite-corner lift. If lightly retained stops slip or allow hatch escape, or tightening is still necessary and produces rocking, this proposed separation of functions fails.
openings.probe: First measure accessible rim underside, edge clearances and stop directions with the ruler. Reject fabrication if two padded clip assemblies cannot capture the rim and constrain the supplied pull direction without touching or trapping the seal. If feasible within ninety minutes, use ten closure/pull trials for this configuration, reopening each cycle and timing one technician. Record position before and after each 20 N pull, corner lift and visible seal damage. Put the 1 mm card at the specified right contact for the tenth, final closure. Require all valued outcomes; stop upon damage. Reserve the two remaining trials for a tighter-clamp rival, including its own disturbed final closure, before the ten-cycle sequence. Those two trials discriminate sensitivity only, not rival durability.
assumptions: Rim underside is accessible and the supplied strips can span the required jaw geometry; these indispensable facts are unprovided.
Four bolts and four pads suffice for two clips, with no permanent deformation or new seal tears.
Clip removal, external cord routing and reinstalling permit an unobstructed opening, thirty-second reopening and ten trials within twenty minutes.
The supplied pull direction can be constrained by the chosen stop locations; stop compliance remains below 1 mm.

artifact.assessment: A fabrication-screened probe, not a deployment claim. Unknown rim geometry may defeat the operation before testing. A damage stop provides protection, not evidence of feasibility.

openings.claim: Separate clearance setting from retention: a card spacer establishes lateral stop clearance during assembly, while straps retain the hatch against separation through independent attachments. Neither function is deleted; the spacer no longer lies in the strap tension path.
openings.delta: Candidate: drill/cut only the aluminum strips into two removable padded rim-clamp assemblies whose projecting edges locate the hatch. Use a supplied 1 mm card sequentially to establish stop clearances, then remove it. Attach the two fabric straps across the 180 mm direction to the clamps; tether removable parts with cord. Comparator: the same clamps and straps, with the clearance card placed beneath one strap contact during closure, coupling spacer placement to retention pressure. Do not restore this coupling in the candidate.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: clamp friction and strap tension alone explain stability; spacer-path separation adds nothing. Candidate predicts less opposite-corner lift than the coupled comparator at comparable strap tension, while meeting position, pull, reopening and seal requirements. Equal lift or worse displacement defeats the proposed benefit; inconsistent hand tension leaves interpretation uncertain.
openings.probe: First verify accessible rim undersides, clamp grip, strap reach and stop placement outside the seal footprint without altering hatch or trough. If feasible, conduct two comparator closure/pull trials, one centered and one with the required right-rim card. Then conduct ten candidate opening/closure/pull cycles, disturbing the final closure. Record ruler displacement and corner lift, 20 N pull response, stopwatch reopening time and visible seal tears. Candidate passes only all specified outcomes after ten cycles. Comparator supplies a limited contrast, not ten-cycle durability evidence.
assumptions: Rim cross-section, hatch thickness and attachment clearance are unspecified; supplied strips, six bolts and four pads must form stable removable clamps and lateral stops.
Both 250 mm straps must reach secure attachments across the hatch without powered assistance.
Comparable manual tension is not instrumented; two comparator trials cannot establish reliable causal performance.
Fabrication must fit ninety minutes and observations twenty minutes; poor grip, obstructed opening, seal damage or unavailable geometry defeats this candidate without relaxing constraints.

artifact.assessment: A bounded link-break probe, not a deployed joint. Geometric feasibility and informative tension matching remain unproven; twelve trials allocate ten-cycle evidence only to the candidate.

openings.claim: Route retaining-strap tension through removable strip-mounted clearance stops. Coupling might limit the supplied corner-lift failure while retaining the hatch; physical synergy is unmeasured.
openings.delta: A retains against separation; B sets repeatable clearance. Change their interface: padded, removable rim saddles carry strap attachments and strip/bolt stops outside the seal. The stop reacts strap compression before excessive corner loading. Release straps and lift all carriers clear; cord retains recoverable loose parts outside the opening.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: ordinary strap friction plus independently useful spacers explains improvement. Coupling predicts intact A×B produces less pull displacement and opposite-corner lift than an otherwise identical link-broken assembly, beyond the gains observed for A alone and B alone. Equal results defeat a coupling claim; increased lift or seal damage defeats this design.
openings.probe: First check rim access, attachment reach and stop placement with ruler; abandon fabrication if supplied materials cannot form stable removable saddles. Compare untreated baseline, A alone, B alone, intact A×B and link-broken A×B. For link-broken, preserve straps, stops, carriers and clearances but redirect strap reaction onto the rim, bypassing stops. Use two trials per baseline/parent control and three per complete configuration: twelve closure/pull trials, including one card-disturbed trial in each complete configuration. Record 20 N displacement, corner lift, reopening time, seal tears, fabrication/setup minutes and reset burden. This screens coupling only; it cannot establish ten-cycle durability within this allocation.
assumptions: Unspecified rim geometry permits padded saddles and both force paths using supplied strips, bolts and 250 mm straps within ninety minutes.
Parent-ablation controls are permitted alongside the two alternative complete joint configurations; otherwise the five-state comparison exceeds the configuration allowance.
Stops can contact outside the seal without permanent deformation; attachment stability and useful stop clearance remain unknown.

artifact.assessment: Keep the original ten-cycle, 1 mm, 20 N and thirty-second outcome as acceptance criteria. This uncertain screening hypothesis grants no deployment permission or proven performance. Setup feasibility, trial-cap interpretation and durability remain unresolved.

openings.claim: The known spacer function may establish repeatable lateral clearance for hatch seating without increased downward corner pressure.
openings.delta: Replace dependence on marker-only centering with opposed corner spacer faces carried by removable brackets made from the supplied strips. Drill or notch strips only; use bolts and rubber pads to seat bracket pairs against the rim. No strap function is proposed.
openings.prediction: Against the ordinary rival of manually centering the untreated hatch, bounded spacer clearance should reduce displacement from the stipulated 4 mm to at most 1 mm under 20 N. If corner lift persists without increased downward pressure, lateral spacers have not resolved that disturbance. These are predictions, not observations.
openings.probe: First dry-fit the four strips as two opposed corner brackets, checking clearance in both lateral axes, rim engagement and removal. Proceed only if the assembly can resist sideways loading without modifying the fixture or obstructing the open aperture. Allocate ten closure/pull trials to ten spacer opening cycles, including the right-contact card on final closure; use two untreated rival trials, one disturbed. Record position, 20 N displacement, corner lift, visible seal damage and full reopening time, including bracket removal onto the tabletop. Limit fabrication to ninety minutes and observation to twenty minutes. Failure to complete these measurements defeats the probe, regardless of stopping on time.
assumptions: Rim geometry permits padded bolted brackets and opposing spacer faces; that geometry is unspecified.
Four strips and six bolts suffice to establish clearances and react 20 N without permanent deformation; capacity is unmeasured.
Brackets can be removed within thirty seconds while all loose parts remain recoverable and the marked opening stays unobstructed.
The disturbed right contact does not invalidate lateral seating or tear the seal. Any failed outcome defeats this configuration; no constraint relaxation is authorized.

artifact.assessment: A spacer-only candidate with an ordinary rival and finite comparison. Feasibility depends on unprovided rim geometry and bracket capacity; this is a probe proposal, not deployment or demonstrated performance.

openings.claim: Two removable padded strip jaws at opposite sides could resist lateral slip while distributing compression; feasibility depends on accessible rim geometry.
openings.delta: Change the carrier from a strap alone to two upper/lower aluminum-strip pairs, each bolted outside the hatch and trough. Capture rubber pads between jaws and surfaces without adhesive. Mark jaw placement and tighten alternately rather than loading the left corner alone. Remove both assemblies completely for inspection; keep bolts, nuts and pads together using cord loops and recover them beside the fixture.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, strap-only friction retention, distributed jaws should reduce lateral displacement without reproducing the opposite-corner lift. Success requires position error at most 1 mm after ten openings, resistance to 20 N, reopening within 30 seconds, and no new visible seal tears, including the final right-contact card disturbance. This is an unmeasured prediction; straps could perform equally well.
openings.probe: First use ruler and loose strip placement to determine whether two padded jaws can straddle hatch and rim with every bolt outside existing material and without permanent deformation. If feasible, drill only the strips and fabricate within ninety minutes. Conduct ten opening/closure/pull cycles within twenty observation minutes, with the supplied 1 mm card at the marked right contact on the final closure. Record position, corner lift, reopening time and visible seal condition each cycle; stop on damage or inability to seat. This uses one configuration and ten of twelve allowed trials. It tests outcome feasibility, but does not establish superiority over the untested strap rival.
assumptions: Accessible underside and outboard bolt clearance are indispensable and unprovided.
Four strips and six bolts must accommodate two jaws without additional carriers.
Rubber friction, strip stiffness and seal-safe clamping force are unknown.
Defeat conditions include jaw slip, card-induced rocking, opposite-corner lift, damage, fabrication overrun or reopening over thirty seconds.

artifact.assessment: A bounded candidate probe, not deployment. If the geometry check fails, no feasible joint is established from the supplied resources; do not alter the hatch, rim, seal or opening to rescue it.
